findings.where: README.md, Quick start, last paragraph: "and the `train` extra installs only on Linux"
findings.finding: This is factually imprecise. In pyproject.toml only `bitsandbytes` in the `train` extra has the marker `platform_system == 'Linux'`. accelerate, datasets, peft, trackio, transformers and trl install on any platform, and no [tool.uv] environment restriction exists. What is true is that 4-bit QLoRA training needs bitsandbytes, which installs only on Linux.
findings.discharge: Reword, for example: "the `train` extra's 4-bit dependency (bitsandbytes) installs only on Linux".

findings.where: README.md, Related work: "The certification method follows conformal risk control (Angelopoulos et al., 2024)."
findings.finding: This overstates how closely the method follows the cited work. The certifier is a high-probability test: an empirical-Bernstein or Hoeffding upper bound on risk, a Clopper-Pearson lower bound on acceptance, and a Bonferroni-corrected audit (certification.py, method 'hoeffding-clopper-pearson-bonferroni'). It is not CRC's expected-loss conformal adjustment. The paper's own framing (uncertainlp-2026-short.tex l.61-63) is "Distribution-free risk control \cite{angelopoulos2024crc} reports certified acceptance". The README's "follows" is stronger than that. The Kotte sentence matches the .bib title, and the "source document as the unit" sentence matches tex l.37-38 and l.79-81.
findings.discharge: Align the wording with the tex, for example: "The certification is a form of distribution-free risk control (Angelopoulos et al., 2024)".
